programs.nl_rule:
The input is a 2×2 grid containing four distinct colors, one per cell.

Create a 6×6 output grid by tiling the 2×2 input in a checkerboard pattern of tiles. Repeat the original 2×2 tile 3 times across to fill each row pair. For even row-pairs (rows 0-1 and 4-5), use the original tile as-is. For odd row-pairs (rows 2-3), use the tile with its two columns swapped (i.e., the left and right columns exchange positions). This produces an alternating tile pattern vertically.

The output grid is 6 rows by 6 columns, exactly 3× the input width and 3× the input height. It is fully filled with no background color — every cell is determined by the tiling rule.

Let's do two demos? Maybe first show_example [[1,2],[3,4]]. Second show_transformed_input [[7,8],[9,6]]. Then query [[2,3],[4,1]]. If correct start.

But note: show_transformed_input shows gold output, but we don't see gold? Actually environment applies verifier and shows pair to student. We might not get output. That's fine. But we need know if accepted? It says "The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student." We get? Probably a success ack or maybe pair? Not sure. Alternatively use show_example to receive success ack. We can compute output. Let's use show_example for both to know they were accepted. Need ensure correct.

Maybe use one demo and one query to reduce calls. But the instruction "A demonstration or probe that is a near-copy of an input already shown or probed is held once: vary the instance." Could mean if we show same input again, it's held. We won't.

2 3

tools.name: show_example

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.

content.text: Now query student on unseen input. Need compute. Let's use [[2,3],[4,1]]. Query.
